en.sup: Supplied in English. The one 'not' at the start of the verse governs both halves of the question.

01.r: Makes the question one that expects the answer yes: of course it was yours.
01.n: Abbott-Smith: a strengthened 'not', used more often in questions where an affirmative answer is expected.

02.r: While the land was still unsold.
02.n: A present participle of the same verb as the main verb that follows: literally 'remaining, did it not remain to you?'. The BSB turns it into 'before it was sold'.

03.n: A dative of the owner: 'remain to you', that is, remain yours.

04.r: The land stayed his own as long as he kept it.
04.n: Abbott-Smith: 'to stay, abide, remain'. An imperfect: it went on being his.

05.r: Joins the time before the sale to the time after it.

06.r: Once the land had been sold.
06.n: An aorist passive participle, literally 'having been sold'. Abbott-Smith cites this verse under 'to sell', with the thing sold.

07.r: Within the range of his own control.

09.r: His own, and no one else's, to decide.
09.n: Abbott-Smith: the possessive 'thy, thine'. The speaker uses the possessive adjective rather than the plain pronoun; a reasonable reading is that it stresses 'your own', as the KJV and Geneva render it.

10.r: He was free to do with the money as he chose.
10.n: Abbott-Smith relates it to ἔξεστι, 'it is permitted', and gives the proper sense as 'liberty or power to act, freedom to exercise the inward force'. So the point is his right to decide, not merely his ability.

11.r: Says where the proceeds stood: under his control.
11.n: A fuller verb for 'to be'; an imperfect.

12.r: Asks for the cause of what he did.

13.r: With 'why', forms the question 'why is it that'.
13.n: Literally 'what (is it) that', a compressed way of asking why.

14.r: He settled on the plan in his own mind.
14.n: Literally 'you placed in your heart'. Abbott-Smith gives the verb's root sense as 'to place, lay, set'; here it is middle, putting something in one's own heart, that is, resolving on it. The older translations' 'conceived' is an interpretation.

16.r: The article with 'heart', where English says 'your heart'.

17.r: The seat of his thinking and choosing.
17.n: Abbott-Smith gives the bodily organ first, then the heart 'in a psychological sense, the seat of man's collective energies, the focus of personal life'.

19.r: The article with 'deed', where English says 'this deed'.

20.r: The act of deceit he planned and carried out.
20.n: Abbott-Smith derives it from πράσσω, to do, and lists this verse under 'that which has been done, a deed, act'. The older translations' 'thing' follows his second sense, 'a thing, matter'.

21.r: Points to what he has just done.

22.r: Denies flatly that the lie was only to men.

23.r: His false show was a lie, told by action.
23.n: Abbott-Smith notes the verb is always in the middle form in the New Testament, and records it with a dative of the person lied to, as here.

24.r: To human beings, as against God.
24.n: A plural of ἄνθρωπος, the general word for human beings, set here against God.

25.r: Sets God against men as the one really lied to.
25.n: Abbott-Smith calls it an adversative particle stronger than δέ.

26.r: The article with 'God', not translated in English.

27.r: God himself was the one deceived.
